import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    dim_customer = inputs["dim_customer"].copy()
    stg_customer = inputs["stg_customer"].copy()
    fact_txn = inputs["fact_txn"].copy()

    # Ensure proper dtypes
    dim_customer["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_customer["eff_start_date"])
    dim_customer["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_customer["eff_end_date"])
    stg_customer["update_date"] = pd.to_datetime(stg_customer["update_date"])
    fact_txn["txn_date"] = pd.to_datetime(fact_txn["txn_date"])

    # Determine max surrogate key before load
    if len(dim_customer) > 0:
        max_sk = dim_customer["customer_sk"].max()
    else:
        max_sk = 0

    # Build lookup of current rows per customer_id
    current_rows = dim_customer[dim_customer["is_current"] == 1].set_index(
        "customer_id", drop=False
    )

    def segment_differs(cur_seg, new_seg):
        cur_is_na = pd.isna(cur_seg)
        new_is_na = pd.isna(new_seg)
        if cur_is_na and new_is_na:
            return False
        if cur_is_na != new_is_na:
            return True
        return cur_seg != new_seg

    creates_list = []
    for _, srow in stg_customer.iterrows():
        cid = srow["customer_id"]
        if cid not in current_rows.index:
            creates = True
        else:
            cur_seg = current_rows.loc[cid, "segment"]
            creates = segment_differs(cur_seg, srow["segment"])
        creates_list.append(creates)

    stg_customer = stg_customer.reset_index(drop=True)
    stg_customer["_creates"] = creates_list

    creating = stg_customer[stg_customer["_creates"]].copy()
    creating = creating.sort_values(by="customer_id", kind="mergesort").reset_index(
        drop=True
    )
    creating["_row_number"] = range(1, len(creating) + 1)
    creating["customer_sk"] = max_sk + creating["_row_number"]

    # Work on a mutable copy of dim_customer to expire rows
    dim_out = dim_customer.copy()

    # Expire current rows for customers that get a new version
    for _, crow in creating.iterrows():
        cid = crow["customer_id"]
        if cid in current_rows.index:
            idx = dim_out[
                (dim_out["customer_id"] == cid) & (dim_out["is_current"] == 1)
            ].index
            dim_out.loc[idx, "eff_end_date"] = crow["update_date"]
            dim_out.loc[idx, "is_current"] = 0

    # Build new version rows
    if len(creating) > 0:
        new_rows = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "customer_sk": creating["customer_sk"].values,
                "customer_id": creating["customer_id"].values,
                "segment": creating["segment"].values,
                "eff_start_date": creating["update_date"].values,
                "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                "is_current": 1,
            }
        )
    else:
        new_rows = pd.DataFrame(
            columns=[
                "customer_sk",
                "customer_id",
                "segment",
                "eff_start_date",
                "eff_end_date",
                "is_current",
            ]
        )

    dim_customer_out = pd.concat([dim_out, new_rows], ignore_index=True, sort=False)

    # Ensure proper dtypes after concat
    dim_customer_out["customer_sk"] = dim_customer_out["customer_sk"].astype("int64")
    dim_customer_out["customer_id"] = dim_customer_out["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    dim_customer_out["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(
        dim_customer_out["eff_start_date"]
    )
    dim_customer_out["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(
        dim_customer_out["eff_end_date"]
    )
    dim_customer_out["is_current"] = dim_customer_out["is_current"].astype("int64")

    # STEP 2: Key the facts against the updated dimension
    merged = fact_txn.merge(
        dim_customer_out[
            ["customer_sk", "customer_id", "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date"]
        ],
        on="customer_id",
        how="left",
        suffixes=("", "_dim"),
    )

    start_ok = merged["eff_start_date"] <= merged["txn_date"]
    end_ok = merged["eff_end_date"].isna() | (
        merged["txn_date"] < merged["eff_end_date"]
    )
    mask = start_ok & end_ok

    merged["_matched_sk"] = np.where(mask, merged["customer_sk"], np.nan)

    grouped = merged.groupby("txn_id", sort=False).agg(
        amount=("amount", "first"), matched_sk=("_matched_sk", "max")
    )

    grouped["customer_sk"] = grouped["matched_sk"].fillna(-1).astype("int64")

    fact_txn_keyed = grouped.reset_index()[["txn_id", "customer_sk", "amount"]]

    # Preserve original order of fact_txn
    order = fact_txn[["txn_id"]].copy()
    order["_order"] = range(len(order))
    fact_txn_keyed = fact_txn_keyed.merge(order, on="txn_id", how="left")
    fact_txn_keyed = fact_txn_keyed.sort_values("_order").drop(columns="_order")
    fact_txn_keyed = fact_txn_keyed.reset_index(drop=True)

    return {
        "dim_customer_out": dim_customer_out,
        "fact_txn_keyed": fact_txn_keyed,
    }
